title: Task-Aware Early Termination for HNSW via Label-Histogram Stabilization

contributions.purpose: Reduce HNSW search latency when downstream tasks only need label correctness, not exact neighbor identities.
contributions.mechanism: A training-free early exit criterion that computes the L1 distance between consecutive top-K label histograms at checkpoints and terminates when it falls below a K-scaled threshold (tau = 4/K, about 2 label swaps).
contributions.evaluation: On the Iceberg ImageNet-EVA02 benchmark, achieves 58.6% p50 and 55.9% p99 latency reduction vs fixed-efSearch baselines while preserving Label Recall@100 within 0.01 percentage points.
contributions.source_quote: A training-free, task-aware early termination criterion for HNSW search that monitors label histogram stability rather than neighbor ID stability.

contributions.purpose: Establish that labels are a coarser, faster-converging signal than neighbor IDs during graph traversal.
contributions.mechanism: Empirical analysis of HNSW traversal showing aggregate label histograms converge while individual neighbor IDs keep changing.
contributions.evaluation: Label distributions stabilize before exact neighbor identities, enabling earlier termination without sacrificing task-relevant recall.
contributions.source_quote: Empirical demonstration that label distributions stabilize before exact neighbor identities, enabling earlier termination without sacrificing task-relevant recall.

contributions.purpose: Quantify the latency advantage of label-stability early exit over ID-stability approaches.
contributions.mechanism: Comprehensive evaluation against fixed-efSearch and ID-stability (Patience-in-Proximity style) baselines at matched checkpoint intervals, including robustness analysis across query difficulties.
contributions.evaluation: 58.6% p50 latency reduction and 19.5% lower p99 latency than ID-stability baselines without sacrificing task-relevant recall.
contributions.source_quote: Comprehensive evaluation showing 58.6% p50 latency reduction and 19.5% lower p99 latency than ID-stability baselines, with robustness across query difficulties.

self_declared_provenance.quote: This observation motivates our work: if downstream tasks care about label correctness rather than exact neighbor identities, early termination should be guided by label stability rather than ID stability. To our knowledge, we are the first to propose a label-based stability criterion for early termination, enabling task-aware search without requiring model training.
All these methods optimize for traditional Recall@K (exact neighbor matching) and are agnostic to downstream task requirements.
